name: INS Mahendragiri

header.one_liner: Final Nilgiri-class P17A stealth frigate; commissioned 13 Jan 2026 at Mumbai; MDL-built; 6,670t full load; BrahMos + Barak-8/ER; the class's lead ship (Nilgiri) commissioned Dec 2025.
header.indigenous_label: ~75% indigenous content (P17A claim); propulsion GE LM2500, weapons partially imported

at_a_glance.Propulsion: COGAG — 2x GE LM2500 gas turbines + 2x MAN diesel engines
at_a_glance.Main_armament: 32-cell VLS (16 BrahMos + 16 Barak-8/ER) — 8 VL-SRSAM on P17A variant fit
at_a_glance.ASW: Twin 324mm torpedo tubes + RBU-6000 ASW rocket launcher + Kamov Ka-28 or MH-60R helicopter
at_a_glance.Radar: BEL MF-STAR with indigenised AESA + IAI EL/M-2248 MF-STAR technology
at_a_glance.Class_size: 7 ships (Nilgiri, Udaygiri, Taragiri, Himgiri, Dunagiri, Mahendragiri, Vindhyagiri)

what_it_is.prose: INS Mahendragiri is the seventh and final Nilgiri-class Project 17A (P17A) stealth frigate, built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) in Mumbai. She follows the lead ship Nilgiri (commissioned December 2025) and sisters Udaygiri, Taragiri, Himgiri, Dunagiri and Vindhyagiri. The P17A is a substantially revised follow-on of the earlier Talwar/Shivalik classes, with a fully stealth-optimised hull and superstructure, integrated platform management system, and ~75% indigenous content claimed by the yard. The class centres on a COGAG propulsion arrangement (two GE LM2500 gas turbines plus two MAN diesels) and carries a 32-cell vertical launch system firing BrahMos anti-ship/land-attack cruise missiles and Barak-8/ER surface-to-air missiles, a 76mm main gun, close-in weapon systems, torpedo tubes and an ASW rocket launcher, plus a multi-role helicopter. Mahendragiri was commissioned on 13 January 2026 at MDL, Mumbai, in the presence of the Chief of the Naval Staff, completing the seven-ship P17A programme (the two Garden Reach-built ships, Vindhyagiri and one other, versus five MDL ships — the class is split across MDL and GRSE). The frigate is named after a mountain peak in Odisha.

deployments_procurement.summary: The P17A programme was sanctioned in 2015 for seven frigates at a combined cost of ~₹45,000 crore across MDL (5) and GRSE (2). INS Mahendragiri was launched in 2023 and commissioned on 13 January 2026 at MDL Mumbai. As the final vessel of the class she completes the seven-ship programme; the fleet is expected to reinforce the Eastern and Western Naval Commands for seaboard defence, air-defence escort and anti-ship/land-attack strike.

faq.question: Was INS Mahendragiri the last Nilgiri-class frigate?
faq.answer: Yes. Mahendragiri, commissioned on 13 January 2026, is the seventh and final Nilgiri-class Project 17A stealth frigate, completing the seven-ship programme (five built at MDL Mumbai and two at GRSE Kolkata).

faq.question: What weapons does INS Mahendragiri carry?
faq.answer: The P17A carries a 32-cell vertical launch system for BrahMos anti-ship/land-attack cruise missiles and Barak-8/ER surface-to-air missiles, a 76mm main gun, AK-630 close-in weapon systems, twin 324mm torpedo tubes, an RBU-6000 ASW rocket launcher and a multi-role ASW helicopter (Ka-28 family or MH-60R).

faq.question: How indigenous is the Nilgiri class?
faq.answer: The P17A is claimed as ~75% indigenous by content, with an indigenous hull, integrated platform management system and 32-cell VLS. Key imports remain the GE LM2500 gas turbines, the IAI radar technology and the Barak-8 missile missile components.
